newsitem.title: UK: Rank five months' operating profits rise. [CORRECTED 08:09 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Rank five months' operating profits rise. [CORRECTED 08:09 GMT]

text.p: British leisure company Rank Group Plc, striking a definitive deal to sell the rest of Rank Xerox (corrects to make clear that Rank is selling its stake in Rank Xerox), said on Friday its operating profits from continuing businesses rose by 7.0 percent in the first five months of the year.
Rank also said its turnover in continuing businesses increased 10 percent at constant exchange rates, while the underlying growth was about one percent for the five months to May 31.

Rank also said it had signed a definitive deal to sell its remaining 20 percent stake in Rank Xerox to Xerox Corp for up to 1.0 billion pounds ($1.6 billion) in cash, as previously agreed by the two joint venture partners.
The company said the disposal would have a broadly neutral effect on 1997 earnings before exceptionals.
Rank also reiterated that it planned to return up to 250 million pounds of the cash to shareholders by way of a share buyback later in the year.
First-quarter revenues at Rank Xerox, an office equipment venture, fell by 10 percent after currency translation, but rose by 3.0 percent on an underlying basis, Rank said.
Meanwhile, the venture's contribution to participation profit dropped by almost a third in the quarter, mainly due to the currency impact.
"There has been no material change to Rank Xerox's trading since the end of the first quarter," Rank said in its statement.
Rank's shares dropped 21.5 pence to 404 by 0735 GMT.

Regarding overall operations, Rank said higher profit at its Hard Rock Cafes, Holidays and Leisure businesses was partly offset by a lower result in Film and Entertainment services due in part to the timing of video releases.
Rank agreed earlier this month to sell its Rank Xerox stake as part of its plan to focus on leisure and entertainment. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
